source_evidence.observation: The paper begins with the abstract ODE u_t = F(u), without declaring the state space, dimension, domain, codomain, or norm.

Equation (1.1) defines an s-stage Runge-Kutta method with A of size s by s and b of length s. The Introduction states that mixed-precision stability is not rigorously studied and that all expectations concerning global errors are valid only under an assumption of stability.

source_evidence.anchor: perturbation definition (2.3) and surrounding one-step discussion
source_evidence.observation: The perturbation is defined by tau(u) = (F(u) - F^epsilon(u))/epsilon. The motivating example distinguishes full-, reduced-, and mixed-precision one-step outputs and calls O(epsilon Delta t^2) a one-step error and O(epsilon Delta t) its global contribution.
The general s-stage scheme combines F with F^epsilon using coefficient pairs (A,b) and (A^epsilon,b^epsilon). It requires, for any y, F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon).

source_evidence.anchor: rewritten scheme (3.2a)-(3.2b), expansion (3.3), and local/global error paragraph
source_evidence.observation: The paper sets A-tilde = A + A^epsilon and b-tilde = b + b^epsilon, but prints the perturbation terms in (3.2) with a plus sign. It decomposes the one-step error as E = E_sch + E_per = O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)); only if the method is stable does it predict global Error = O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m).

source_evidence.anchor: third-order perturbation table and smooth-versus-chopped regularity discussion
source_evidence.observation: The perturbation expansion contains terms through third order in both Delta t and epsilon. In the smooth scenario, F and F^epsilon are called well behaved and all their derivatives are assumed to exist and be bounded. For chopping, F^epsilon = Chop(F) is described as bounded but non-Lipschitz, tau is non-Lipschitz, its derivatives may not exist, and componentwise zero conditions replace cancellations.

source_evidence.anchor: consistency conditions and nonsmooth perturbation conditions (3.4a)-(3.4g)
source_evidence.observation: The page gives the complete consistency hierarchy and the absolute-value perturbation conditions for non-well-behaved tau. Through consistency order three these are b-tilde e = 1, b-tilde c-tilde = 1/2, b-tilde(c-tilde dot c-tilde) = 1/3, and b-tilde A-tilde c-tilde = 1/6.
For well-behaved tau, the paper lists all cancellation conditions through perturbation order m = 3, grouped under unexplained labels 'for n >= 1', 'for n >= 2', and 'for n >= 3'.
The novel methods are said to have been developed with an optimization code similar to those described in reference [10]; no exact algebraic coefficient source is identified there.

A displayed example places c and c^epsilon beside A and A^epsilon consistently with the conventional row-sum interpretation c = Ae and c^epsilon = A^epsilon e, although the paper does not separately state this as a general definition.

Section 4.3 contrasts earlier methods satisfying the stricter conditions (3.4) with Method 4s3pC, which is devised to satisfy the less restrictive conditions (3.5) applicable only when tau is well behaved.

source_evidence.anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display and the two Error formulas
source_evidence.observation: The paper displays the Method 4s3pC coefficients, including b^epsilon = (0,0,0,0), followed by Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3) for well-behaved tau and Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2) when tau is not well behaved. It then introduces a periodic diffusion-equation experiment.

The centered-difference perturbation is identified as well behaved and is said to produce the expected third-order perturbation rate. The chopped Fourier perturbation is identified as not well behaved and is said to match the expected second-order perturbation rate. The paper warns that using two different spatial operators is highly sensitive, requires careful stability analysis, and is not recommended generally without rigorous justification.
The paper says that epsilon is treated as a single constant upper bound and leaves varying orders of epsilon to future work.

binders: The generic evolution problem is u_t = F(u), with u and F otherwise untyped; no state dimension or state space is bound. [PDF p. 1, anchor: opening ODE in Section 1]

The generic additive method has s stages, stage indices i,j = 1,...,s, matrices A and A^epsilon of size s by s, weights b and b^epsilon of length s, step size Delta t, states u^n,u^(n+1), and stages y^(i). [PDF p. 2, anchor: equation (1.1); PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

Method 4s3pC has four displayed weight entries and coefficient rows indexed 1 through 4, hence is presented as a four-stage instance of the generic scheme. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display]

The approximation requirement is stated with quantifier order 'for any y' followed by F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon); no norm or uniformity qualification follows it. [PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph following (3.1)]

p denotes classical consistency order and m denotes perturbation order in O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)) at one step. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency and (3.4)]

The symbol n in the labels 'for n >= 1', 'for n >= 2', and 'for n >= 3' in (3.4) and (3.5) is not defined in the surrounding text; the preceding expansion suggests, but does not state, that it tracks powers epsilon^n. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation expansion table; PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: (3.4) and (3.5)]
hypotheses: The additive scheme is y^(i) = u^n + Delta t sum_j A_ij F(y^(j)) + Delta t sum_j A^epsilon_ij F^epsilon(y^(j)) and u^(n+1) = u^n + Delta t sum_j b_j F(y^(j)) + Delta t sum_j b^epsilon_j F^epsilon(y^(j)). [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

F^epsilon approximates F with F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon) for any y, and tau is normalized as tau(u) = (F(u) - F^epsilon(u))/epsilon. [PDF p. 3, anchor: (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph following (3.1)]

All global Error formulas inherit the standing condition that the relevant perturbed method is stable; the paper does not prove that condition for Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 2, anchor: Introduction stability caveat; PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 19, anchor: stability warning after Figure 6]

For the well-behaved regime, the stated analytic context is that F and F^epsilon are well-behaved functions whose derivatives all exist and are bounded, so tau and its derivatives are treated as bounded and coefficient-level cancellations are permitted. [PDF p. 6, anchor: smooth regularity discussion]

For the non-well-behaved regime exemplified by chopping, F^epsilon = Chop(F) is bounded but not Lipschitz, tau is not Lipschitz, its derivatives may not exist, and Taylor expansion about tau cannot be used as in the smooth case. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping and non-Lipschitz discussion]

The cumulative consistency conditions through order three are: for p >= 1, b-tilde e = 1; for p >= 2, b-tilde c-tilde = 1/2; for p >= 3, b-tilde(c-tilde dot c-tilde) = 1/3 and b-tilde A-tilde c-tilde = 1/6. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions preceding Section 3.1.1]
The complete smooth conditions for m >= 1 are (3.5a): under the paper's label n >= 1, b^epsilon e = 0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: (3.5a)]

The additional smooth conditions for m >= 2 are (3.5b), under n >= 1: b^epsilon c-tilde = 0 and b-tilde c^epsilon = 0; and (3.5c), under n >= 2: b^epsilon c^epsilon = 0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: (3.5b)-(3.5c)]

The additional smooth conditions for m >= 3 are (3.5d), under n >= 1: b^epsilon A-tilde c-tilde = 0, b-tilde A^epsilon c-tilde = 0, b-tilde A-tilde c^epsilon = 0, b^epsilon(c-tilde dot c-tilde) = 0, and b-tilde(c-tilde dot c^epsilon) = 0; (3.5e), under n >= 2: b^epsilon A^epsilon c-tilde = 0, b^epsilon A-tilde c^epsilon = 0, b-tilde A^epsilon c^epsilon = 0, b^epsilon(c^epsilon dot c-tilde) = 0, and b-tilde(c^epsilon dot c^epsilon) = 0; and (3.5f), under n >= 3: b^epsilon A^epsilon c^epsilon = 0 and b^epsilon(c^epsilon dot c^epsilon) = 0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: (3.5d)-(3.5f)]
The complete nonsmooth conditions for m >= 1 are (3.4a), under n >= 1: |b^epsilon||e| = 0. [PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4a)]
The additional nonsmooth conditions for m >= 2 are (3.4b), under n >= 1: |b-tilde||c^epsilon| = 0. [PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4b)]

The additional nonsmooth conditions for m >= 3 are (3.4c), under n >= 1: |b-tilde||A-tilde||c^epsilon| = 0 and |b-tilde|(|c-tilde| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0; and (3.4d), under n >= 2: |b-tilde|(|c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0. [PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4c)-(3.4d)]

The additional nonsmooth conditions for m >= 4 are (3.4e), under n >= 1: |b-tilde||A-tilde||A-tilde||c^epsilon| = 0, |b-tilde||A-tilde|(|c-tilde| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0, |b-tilde|(|A-tilde||c^epsilon| dot |c-tilde|) = 0, |b-tilde|(|A-tilde||c-tilde| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0, and |b-tilde|(|c^epsilon| dot |c-tilde| dot |c-tilde|) = 0; (3.4f), under n >= 2: |b-tilde||A-tilde|(|c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0, |b-tilde|(|A-tilde||c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0, and |b-tilde|(|c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon| dot |c-tilde|) = 0; and (3.4g), under n >= 3: |b-tilde|(|c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon| dot |c^epsilon|) = 0. [PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4e)-(3.4g)]
conclusions: For well-behaved tau, Section 4.3 explicitly prints Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3). By the paper's notation this is a global error form, not a local one, and it is an expectation conditional on stability rather than a separately stated theorem. [PDF p. 18, anchor: first Method 4s3pC Error formula; PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 19, anchor: 'as expected' discussion]

When tau is not well behaved, Section 4.3 explicitly prints Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2). This is likewise a global, stability-conditional expected error form rather than a theorem. [PDF p. 18, anchor: second Method 4s3pC Error formula; PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 19, anchor: 'matches our expected error' discussion]

Applying the general one-step/global correspondence, the well-behaved formula corresponds to an inferred one-step form E = O(Delta t^4) + O(epsilon Delta t^4), while the non-well-behaved formula corresponds to inferred E = O(Delta t^4) + O(epsilon Delta t^3); these local formulas are not separately displayed in Section 4.3. [PDF p. 5, anchor: E and Error formulas; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC Error formulas]

The diffusion experiment reports behavior consistent with the displayed expectations: the centered-difference perturbation is associated with the epsilon Delta t^3 global term, while chopped Fourier evaluation with epsilon = 10^-4 initially behaves at third order and then at second order as Delta t decreases. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: Figure 6 caption and following discussion]
definitions_and_conventions: tau(u) is explicitly defined as (F(u) - F^epsilon(u))/epsilon. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3)]
A-tilde = A + A^epsilon and b-tilde = b + b^epsilon. [PDF p. 5, anchor: sentence following (3.2b)]

The paper uses c, c^epsilon, and c-tilde in its conditions without a standalone general definition; displayed Butcher arrays elsewhere support the conventional interpretation c = Ae, c^epsilon = A^epsilon e, and c-tilde = c + c^epsilon = A-tilde e. [PDF p. 11, anchor: Butcher arrays following (4.1)]

The dot in expressions such as c-tilde dot c^epsilon denotes the componentwise product customary in Runge-Kutta order conditions; the paper does not formally define that notation. [PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: consistency conditions, (3.4), and (3.5)]

For nonsmooth conditions, absolute values are used componentwise to force every contributing product to zero rather than merely forcing its signed sum to cancel; the paper illustrates this with b^epsilon_j c_j = 0 and |b^epsilon||c| = 0. [PDF p. 6, anchor: final paragraph before Section 3.1]

E denotes the error at one time step and is split into scheme error E_sch and perturbation error E_per; capitalized Error denotes the predicted accumulated/global error under stability. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following expansion (3.3)]

In the general framework u^n and u^(n+1) denote scheme states without a separate exact-solution symbol; the total error nevertheless includes both consistency and perturbation contributions. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: equations (3.1)-(3.3)]
implicit_context: The B-series displays derivatives F_y, F_yy, F_yyy and, in the smooth case, derivatives of tau, but no formal differentiability class, neighborhood, invariant set, or uniform derivative bound is declared. [PDF pp. 5-6, anchors: B-series tables and regularity discussion]

No state-space dimension, scalar field, state norm, or error norm is specified for the abstract ODE or Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 1, anchor: opening ODE; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC and diffusion test]

The generic global estimate does not state a fixed interval [0,T], a relation N Delta t = T, or uniformity as Delta t tends to zero; the Section 4.3 diffusion experiment also gives no final time. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion experiment]

No theorem, lemma, proposition, or proof is attached to either Section 4.3 Error display; the experimental discussion calls the rates expected. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchors: Method 4s3pC Error displays and Figure 6 discussion]

The stability condition is standing and external to the accuracy calculation: mixed-precision perturbations may invalidate stability, and the paper explicitly says it does not rigorously analyze that issue. [PDF p. 2, anchor: Introduction stability caveat]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Method 4s3pC is an instance of the additive perturbed Runge-Kutta scheme (3.1), designed specifically around the smooth cancellation conditions (3.5), unlike preceding methods designed for the absolute-value conditions (3.4). Its displayed b^epsilon is the zero vector, so the final update has no direct F^epsilon-weighted term, although stages use both A and A^epsilon. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b); PDF p. 17, anchor: opening of Section 4.3; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficients]
numerical_model: epsilon is used as a perturbation-size or implicit-solver-tolerance scale, and F^epsilon is required to differ from F by O(epsilon); it is not formally identified with IEEE unit roundoff. [PDF p. 3, anchor: implicit tolerance and (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: approximation paragraph]
The paper ultimately describes epsilon as one constant upper bound, rather than a stage-dependent or term-dependent family. [PDF p. 20, anchor: continuation of Conclusions]
For mixed-precision chopping, F^epsilon = Chop(F); this operator is described as bounded but non-Lipschitz and tau may lack derivatives. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion]

In the well-behaved Section 4.3 experiment, F is a high-resolution Fourier spectral approximation of u_xx and F^epsilon is a low-resolution centered-difference approximation; the paper asserts their difference is well behaved. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion discretization and Figure 6 discussion]

In the non-well-behaved experiment, F is the double-precision Fourier spectral approximation and F^epsilon is its half-precision chopped output, with epsilon = 10^-4 in the reported mixed-precision run. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Figure 6 caption; PDF p. 19, anchor: chopped-Fourier discussion]

No floating-point rounding mode, relative-versus-absolute rounding rule, unit-roundoff model, accumulation model, or treatment of subnormal and exceptional values is specified. [PDF pp. 3-4, anchors: tolerance/truncation examples; PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion]
error_notions: The formal one-step error is E = E_sch + E_per, combining classical scheme approximation error and perturbation error. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following (3.3)]

If stable, one power of Delta t is lost when passing from one-step E = O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)) to global Error = O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m). [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error formulas]
The Section 4.3 displays use capitalized Error and therefore follow the global side of this convention. [PDF p. 18, anchor: two Method 4s3pC Error formulas; PDF p. 5, anchor: global Error notation]

The numerical Figure 6 uses a double-precision Fourier-spectral implementation as a reference but does not define whether the plotted error is absolute, relative, final-time, maximum-in-time, or measured in a particular vector norm. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Figure 6 caption]

For the PDE experiment, F is already a spatial discretization, so the displayed temporal Error formulas do not explicitly separate temporal error from the Fourier or centered-difference spatial approximation error. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion discretization discussion]
norms: No norm is specified for F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon), for the one-step error E, or for global Error. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: approximation requirement and local/global formulas]
The vertical axis Log_10(Error) in Figure 6 does not define the underlying error norm. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Figure 6]

The bars in (3.4) denote componentwise absolute values of coefficient arrays used to prevent cancellation, not a state-space norm. [PDF p. 6, anchor: componentwise explanation; PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4a)-(3.4g)]
constants_and_indexing: The displayed A^epsilon coefficients are a^epsilon_11 = 0.511243008730995, a^epsilon_21 = -1.999347282862640, a^epsilon_22 = 1.957161067302390, a^epsilon_31 = 0.443312893511937, a^epsilon_32 = -0.573131033672219, a^epsilon_33 = 0.128283796414019, a^epsilon_41 = -2, a^epsilon_42 = -0.160330320741428, a^epsilon_43 = 0.579597314161362, and a^epsilon_44 = 1.484688928981990. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display]
The displayed weights are b = (0.002837446974069, 0.336264433650450, 0.806376720267787, -0.145478600892306) and b^epsilon = (0,0,0,0). [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display]
The paper structurally displays b^epsilon as exactly the zero vector; no approximation sign or nonzero hidden entries are indicated. [PDF p. 18, anchor: b^epsilon display]

The nonzero decimal coefficients are introduced with equality signs and the phrase 'given by the coefficients', but are not labeled exact, rounded, or approximate. No symbolic or higher-precision tableau is identified. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display; PDF p. 10, anchor: optimization-code statement]

Only selected matrix entries are printed rather than full 4 by 4 arrays; interpreting every omitted entry as zero is conventional but not verbally stated in Section 4.3. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display]
Time indexing advances u^n to u^(n+1), while stage indices run from 1 to s; no starting index, number of steps, or final index is fixed for Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

The offsets in the rate correspondence are explicit: local consistency exponent p+1 becomes global p, and local perturbation exponent m+1 becomes global m under stability. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error formulas]
higher_order_terms: Expansion (3.3) is written through second order with a remainder O(Delta t^3), while the subsequent perturbation table is described as extending through third order in both Delta t and epsilon. [PDF pp. 5-6, anchors: (3.3) and perturbation table]

The perturbation table explicitly contains epsilon, epsilon^2, and epsilon^3 terms; the final Method 4s3pC Error formulas display only O(epsilon Delta t^m) contributions and do not separately enumerate higher powers of epsilon. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation table; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC Error formulas]

No constants in any O-term are given, and no dependence of those constants on F, tau, derivative bounds, the state, the time interval, epsilon, spatial resolution, or stability constants is stated. [PDF pp. 4-6, anchors: approximation and error expansions; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC Error formulas]

No two-parameter limiting convention for epsilon and Delta t is stated; epsilon is later described only as a single constant upper bound. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Error formulas; PDF p. 20, anchor: epsilon statement]
exceptional_values: Although tau divides by epsilon, the paper does not explicitly assume epsilon > 0 or epsilon != 0 in the general definition. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3)]
No admissible range for Delta t is stated beyond the external requirement that the method be stable. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph]
No assumptions excluding overflow, underflow, NaN, infinity, subnormal values, or failed implicit solves are stated. [PDF pp. 3-4, anchors: mixed-precision motivating example]
The acknowledged exceptional analytic behavior is the discontinuity/non-Lipschitz character of chopping, for which tau derivatives may not exist. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion]

Using distinct spatial operators for F and F^epsilon carries an additional unproved stability risk, and the paper warns against general use without rigorous justification. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion discretization warning]

undebatable_constraints: Method 4s3pC is intended to have classical consistency order three and to satisfy the smooth perturbation conditions (3.5) through m = 3. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions; PDF pp. 17-18, anchors: Section 4.3 introduction and first Error formula]
The well-behaved-tau claim is the global form Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3). [PDF p. 18, anchor: first Method 4s3pC Error formula; PDF p. 5, anchor: global Error convention]
The non-well-behaved-tau claim is the global form Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 18, anchor: second Method 4s3pC Error formula; PDF p. 5, anchor: global Error convention]

Neither global formula is unconditional: the paper's standing accuracy-to-global-error passage requires stability, and stability is not proved for Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 2, anchor: stability caveat; PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph]
The two formulas are narrative theoretical expectations supported by an experiment, not theorem-stated results. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchors: Error displays and 'expected error' discussion]
All four consistency equations through p = 3 must be retained; neither of the two third-order tree conditions may be dropped. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions]
All parts of (3.5a)-(3.5f), including the epsilon^2- and epsilon^3-grouped conditions, belong to the stated smooth m = 3 hierarchy. [PDF p. 8, anchor: (3.5a)-(3.5f)]

All parts of (3.4a)-(3.4g) are componentwise absolute-value conditions for the nonsmooth hierarchy and are distinct from the smooth cancellation equations. [PDF pp. 6-7, anchors: componentwise explanation and (3.4a)-(3.4g)]
The displayed perturbed update weights satisfy b^epsilon = (0,0,0,0) exactly as printed. [PDF p. 18, anchor: b^epsilon display]

The paper does not provide a formal state space, error norm, O-constant, finite-time horizon, or step-family quantification for the Method 4s3pC rates. [PDF pp. 1, 5, 18-19, anchors: opening ODE, global formula, and diffusion experiment]

The printed nonzero decimal coefficients must not be silently promoted to a separately sourced exact algebraic tableau, because no such tableau or exactness statement appears in the paper. [PDF p. 18, anchor: coefficient display; PDF p. 10, anchor: optimization-code statement]
The centered-difference/Fourier experiment carries an explicit stability warning and is presented only as an illustration. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion discretization warning]

ambiguities.issue: Exact status of the nonzero decimal coefficients
ambiguities.evidence: Section 4.3 says the method 'is given by the coefficients' and uses equality signs, but never calls the decimals exact, approximate, or rounded; the only provenance is a general statement that novel methods used optimization code similar to reference [10]. No symbolic, rational, or higher-precision tableau is identified. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display; PDF p. 10, anchor: opening of Section 4]
ambiguities.impact: The source contracts the displayed digits but does not justify treating them as an exact algebraic solution of the order equations. An exact formalization would need either explicit tolerances or additional coefficient data not supplied by the paper.

ambiguities.issue: Literal displayed decimals do not exactly satisfy at least one claimed smooth cancellation identity
ambiguities.evidence: Using the conventional c^epsilon = A^epsilon e relation illustrated by the paper, the displayed decimal literals give b-tilde c^epsilon = -3.56016364770570e-16 when treated as exact finite decimals, rather than exactly zero as required by (3.5b); b^epsilon is zero, so b-tilde = b. [PDF p. 8, anchor: (3.5b); PDF p. 11, anchor: Butcher-array convention; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficients]
ambiguities.impact: This strongly suggests rounded optimization output, but the paper does not say so or supply the underlying exact values. The intended algebraic condition and the literal decimal tableau therefore cannot both be taken as exact without qualification.

ambiguities.issue: Sign inconsistency in the perturbation rewrite
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.3) defines tau = (F - F^epsilon)/epsilon, hence F^epsilon = F - epsilon tau. Substituting this into the additive scheme (3.1) gives negative epsilon A^epsilon tau and epsilon b^epsilon tau contributions, whereas (3.2a)-(3.2b) print them with plus signs. [PDF p. 3, anchor: (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: (3.1a)-(3.1b); PDF p. 5, anchor: (3.2a)-(3.2b)]
ambiguities.impact: The exact signed decomposition is inconsistent. Replacing tau by -tau repairs it, and the zero coefficient conditions and big-O rates are sign-insensitive, but a source-faithful formalization must not silently assert both definitions simultaneously.

ambiguities.issue: The generic nonsmooth m = 2 condition is not visibly reconciled with the displayed Method 4s3pC tableau
ambiguities.evidence: Condition (3.4b) requires |b-tilde||c^epsilon| = 0 componentwise. Under the conventional c^epsilon = A^epsilon e and omitted-entry-zero reading, the displayed A^epsilon gives c^epsilon = (0.511243008730995, -0.042186215560250, -0.001534343746263, -0.096044077598076), while every displayed component of b = b-tilde is nonzero. Nevertheless Section 4.3 states the generic non-well-behaved global term O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 7, anchor: (3.4b); PDF p. 11, anchor: Butcher-array convention; PDF p. 18, anchors: coefficients and second Error formula]
ambiguities.impact: The displayed data do not establish the claimed generic nonsmooth m = 2 rate through the paper's own sufficient componentwise condition. The rate must be retained as the paper's stated expectation, possibly specific to the tested perturbation, rather than upgraded to a theorem derived from (3.4b).

ambiguities.issue: Meaning of 'well behaved' is qualitative rather than formal
ambiguities.evidence: The paper associates the smooth case with F and F^epsilon having existing bounded derivatives and associates chopping with non-Lipschitz tau, but it specifies no differentiability order, domain, norm, neighborhood, or uniform bounds. [PDF p. 6, anchor: regularity discussion; PDF p. 8, anchor: opening of Section 3.1.2]
ambiguities.impact: The analytic hypothesis cannot be translated into a unique formal predicate without adding choices. At minimum it must support the B-series derivatives and cancellations used through the requested order.

ambiguities.issue: The index n in conditions (3.4) and (3.5) is undefined
ambiguities.evidence: The conditions are labeled 'for n >= 1', 'for n >= 2', and 'for n >= 3' without defining n. The immediately preceding table is organized by epsilon, epsilon^2, and epsilon^3 terms, which suggests an intended association but does not state it. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation table; PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: (3.4) and (3.5)]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should preserve the groupings exactly while marking any interpretation of n as the epsilon-power index as inferred.

ambiguities.issue: O-notation, norm, horizon, and two-parameter quantifiers are absent
ambiguities.evidence: The paper writes F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon), one-step and global error formulas, and the Section 4.3 rates without defining a norm, constants, a fixed time interval, N Delta t = T, or the joint limiting behavior of epsilon and Delta t; epsilon is only later called a single constant upper bound. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: approximation and local/global formulas; PDF p. 18, anchor: Error formulas; PDF p. 20, anchor: epsilon statement]
ambiguities.impact: The source determines exponents but not uniformity, constant dependence, or quantifier order. Those details must remain unspecified rather than being invented.

ambiguities.issue: The spatial-approximation epsilon in the well-behaved experiment is not quantified
ambiguities.evidence: For the centered-difference/Fourier pairing the paper calls the operator difference well behaved and writes an O(epsilon Delta t^3) term, but it does not state how epsilon depends on the two spatial resolutions or give its numerical value for the magenta curve. [PDF pp. 18-19, anchor: diffusion discretization and Figure 6 discussion]
ambiguities.impact: The experiment supports the temporal slope distinction but does not define a reusable quantitative perturbation bound for that operator pair.

ambiguities.evidence: Section 4.3 lists selected a_ij and a^epsilon_ij values rather than printing full matrices or explicitly saying that every unlisted entry is zero. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient display]
ambiguities.impact: The usual lower-triangular omitted-zero interpretation is highly plausible and needed to reconstruct the scheme, but it is inherited convention rather than an explicit sentence in the selected passage.

contract_plain_english: Method 4s3pC is a four-stage additive perturbed Runge-Kutta method intended to satisfy all classical consistency equations through order three and all smooth perturbation equations (3.5) through m = 3. [PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: consistency conditions and (3.5); PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Section 4.3] With sufficiently regular, bounded-derivative tau and a stable global evolution, the paper expects global Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3); when tau is not well behaved, it expects global Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 18, anchor: two Error formulas; PDF p. 5, anchor: stability-conditional global convention] These are global expectations, not local formulas or theorem-stated guarantees; their inferred local counterparts have Delta t exponents one larger. [PDF p. 5, anchor: one-step/global correspondence; PDF p. 19, anchor: expected-error discussion] The full nonsmooth conditions (3.4) use componentwise absolute values because cancellation cannot be justified for chopping, while (3.5) uses signed cancellations when tau is smooth. [PDF pp. 6-8, anchors: regularity discussion, (3.4), and (3.5)] The source prints b^epsilon = (0,0,0,0), but gives the other coefficients only as unqualified decimal displays and identifies no exact underlying tableau; literal decimal arithmetic does not exactly satisfy all claimed zero identities. [PDF p. 18, anchor: coefficient display; PDF p. 10, anchor: optimization-code statement] The paper also leaves the state space, norm, O-constants, finite-time horizon, step family, and floating-point exception model undefined, and its tau definition has the opposite sign from the perturbation terms printed in (3.2). [PDF pp. 1, 3-5, anchors: opening ODE, (2.3), (3.1), and (3.2)]
